text:
A perspective on prevalent community attitudes can be gained by study of the minutes of these sessions. The minutes of all CDBG meetings are on file with the Housing Division of the Department of Property and Code Enforcement. Three meetings in particular are important:
1. Steering Committee public hearing on selection of CDBG Project Area....
November 2, 1977
2. Presentation of proposed CDBG projects in selected CDBG areas  made by citizens....December 10, 1977
3. Steering Committee hearing at which Preliminary CDBG Plan was adopted....
December 19, 1977
A brief synopsis of each of these important citizen meetings follows.
1. At the November 2 hearing, twenty-five speakers representing twelve separate neighborhoods spoke. Each presented a proposal for including a different neighborhood in the new three-year CDBG program. In many cases the proposed target area was an expansion of an existing CNRA under the previous CDBG program. However, several new neighborhoods were suggested for inclusion in the program.
In addition to presenting street boundaries for each proposed area, the speaker also told the Committee what the pressing problems of the neighborhood are and why its inclusion in the CDBG program would be useful. Selected excerpts from the minutes of that meeting are quoted below.
(a) Speaker from Northside area: Homes well over 25 years old. Almost 100% wooden structure. In need of remodeling. Run down and in urgent need of repairs, both interior and exterior. Approximately 18 to 20% elderly, retired people and approximately 80% of people within expanded program would be in favor of this project. Has a petition with twenty-three signatures.
(b) Speaker from Campus area: Homes are deteriorating near campus. Interested in having good environment for San Jose students. If part of the area deteriorates, it is bad for the whole area. Mainly very old houses  Victorian. Divided into 3 or 4 units., considerably run down. Apartment houses in the area also run down. Built 20 years ago. Not asking for capitol improvements. Won't be using much money from single family dwelling funds, primarily would be using Section 312 loans. Want funds to improve area closer to downtown area for University Neighborhood Group and students.
(c) Speaker from Gardner area: Critical housing deterioration. Capitol improvements- storm sewer line, street repairs, park development. Land settling badly. Roads in bad shape, curbs not extended, Gutter non-existent. Sewage backing up into houses. Sidewalks bumpy. One foot difference in sidewalk and street, dangerous for kids and elderly. No street lights. Houses settling and doors won't close. Standing water in streets after rain. Broken foundations because of settling.
Considerable interest in area for expanding boundaries.
